summary: Multiplexed session token rotation causes intermittent truncation on stream resume
description: Issue summary: LexaHealth reports that when multiple chat streams are multiplexed over a single websocket, and the platform performs session-token rotation (security refresh), some clients observe truncated final choices after a resume. Impact: In worst cases the assistant's last sentence is cut off or the final choice is missing, causing downstream UI to show an unfinished answer and triggering duplicate retry logic. Environment: Dedicated cluster for LexaHealth in prod/us-east; traffic uses Reed proxy and connection multiplexing at the customer side.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start two concurrent websocket streams (A and B) to the Redwood hosted endpoint using mux session id. 2) Stream tokens from model redwood-rlhf-13b while sending keepalives. 3) Trigger token rotation by forcing a short-lived session key refresh (simulate by calling the rotate endpoint or wait for scheduled rotation). 4) Simulate a transient disconnect on stream A, allow client to reconnect and resume with resume_offset. 5) Observe that stream A sometimes resumes but final choice is truncated or missing while stream B continues normally.
expected_behavior: On resume, the server should return a complete, stitched stream up to the final "end" event (or final choice) preserving ordering and producing no duplicate or truncated tokens.
logs:
Customer logs: [ws://lexa-prod-conn] resume_request: session_id=abc123, resume_offset=2452
Server logs (approx): 2026-03-05T14:11:10Z session-manager: rotating token for session abc123 -> token tkn_7G
2026-03-05T14:11:11Z mux-router: connection MUX-9: reassigning stream A to worker w-12
2026-03-05T14:11:11Z serving-runtime[w-12]: resume request offset=2452, kv-cache-hit=true, seq_start=2453
2026-03-05T14:11:11Z serving-runtime[w-12]: final-choice emitted (seq=2499) then connection tear-down during send
2026-03-05T14:11:11Z api-gateway: truncated send detected, client ack missing
comments: Support (Aisha): Thanks for the report — we can reproduce locally with a muxed client. Collecting traces and asking SRE to check token rotation path.

Customer (LexaHealth): We see this intermittently during our 04:00-06:00 traffic spike. It's impacting user-visible answers ~0.8% of streams. Priority is high because product blocks on final token for analytics ingestion.

SRE (Marco): Reproduced on dedicated pool. Hypothesis: session token rotation triggers a short window where the mux-router rebinds stream to a different worker but resume_offset is applied relative to the old worker's streaming buffer, producing an off-by-one when KV cache pointer advances during rotation.
Eng (Priya Rao): Adding instrumentation to capture resume_offset, worker_id, and latest-kv-cache-seq in a single trace. Will also add assert checks on resume boundary handling.
Support (Aisha): Noted workaround for customer - disable client-side muxing for critical paths or increase resume window tolerance to 2s until patch rolled out.
Customer (LexaHealth): Applied the workaround and observed immediate drop to ~0.02% of affected streams. Thanks — will hold on full enablement until fix is deployed.
investigation_notes: Initial triage (2026-03-05): Reproduced with synthetic mux client. Observed correlation between token rotation and worker rebind events. Trace show resume_offset=2452 but worker had advanced to seq_start=2453 causing first token after resume to be skipped (off-by-one). Hypotheses: (1) session-manager issues rotation broadcast after mux-router rebind causing stale offset semantics; (2) serving-runtime does not atomically remap resume_offset to new worker's cache base when reattach occurs; (3) network-level partial write during final-choice send leads to missing terminal event on client side. Further tests: instrumented resume path to log (resume_offset, cache_base_seq, worker_id, token_version) — logs attached to PR. Related Slack: #support (thread: https://slack.redwood.ai/thread/GPQ9x2), related incident stub INC-2026-03-05-LEXA.
resolution: Mitigation applied: Increase resume tolerance on mux-router (v2) to accept resume_offset +/-1 for same session; added guard in serving-runtime to re-align resume_offset to target worker's cache_base_seq when worker change detected. Deployed hotfix to dedicated cluster 2026-03-09 (runtime patch release v1.67.2). Post-deploy monitoring: affected streams dropped from 0.8% to 0.01% for LexaHealth in prod/us-east over 72 hours. Follow-ups: engineering to land full fix that ensures atomic token-rotation + rebind ordering (tracked in PR #2291). Customer workaround: disable client-side multiplexing for latency-sensitive flows (documented in runbook). Ticket status: In Progress until full end-to-end integration tests are green and customer approves re-enablement.
next_steps: 1) Eng to complete end-to-end test harness for rotation+rebind (owner: Priya Rao, due 2026-03-15). 2) Add automated end-to-end regression to CI for muxed resumes (owner: Runtime QA). 3) Confirm LexaHealth can re-enable multiplexing in staging and schedule a gradual rollout. 4) Update public runbook and customer-facing KB article summarizing workaround and expected behavior.
notes_for_postmortem: Potential root cause: non-atomic ordering between session token rotation broadcast and mux-router stream rebind which exposes resume_offset semantics that assumed single-worker sticky mapping. Postmortem should review token rotation ordering guarantees, mux-router handoff protocol, and add stricter invariants in serving-runtime. Include customer impact metrics and timeline.
